children.text: A solution containing a mixture of a weak acid and its conjugate base, or a weak base and its conjugate acid, is called a buffer solution. Buffer solutions are essential because they resist significant changes in pH when small amounts of strong acid or base are added. This stability occurs because the weak conjugate acid-base pair neutralizes the added acids or bases, converting them into their weaker conjugate forms and leaving the hydronium ion concentration relatively unchanged.

Buffers are crucial in many real-life applications. For instance, our blood is a natural buffer system that maintains a stable pH to ensure proper physiological function. Similarly, buffers are used in the food industry to maintain the desired pH level in products, ensuring flavor and preservation. In everyday life, swimming pools use buffering agents to keep the water pH balanced, preventing it from becoming too acidic or too basic.
